node.label: David Cannadine
node.date_label: The Decline and Fall of the British Aristocracy (1990) · Class in Britain (1998) · Ornamentalism (2001)
node.description: A historian of modern Britain who connects aristocratic power to urban development and writes biography as a problem of proportion and judgment. His interview explains how aristocratic ground rents and urban growth complicate a simple division between landed elites and the industrial city.

proposed_edges.relationship: Connects aristocratic wealth and power to urban development as well as rural landholding.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview describes Calthorpe ground rents and Edgbaston, motivating a broader social history of aristocracy.

proposed_edges.relationship: Treats biography as a balance of private/public life, evidence, proportion and competing historical judgments.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview’s ODNB and Thatcher answers explain the method; his acknowledgment of underrepresented women/businesspeople concerns an editorial programme, not sole authorship of dictionary lives.
